question: At 14.5 km/h, how did impact forces in thick maximalist running shoes compare with those in conventional running shoes?
answer: About 10% higher. Kulmala's team measured the impact peak 10.7% higher and the loading rate 12.3% higher in the highly cushioned shoe. Runners met the softer sole by stiffening their legs, so the body came down harder on top of the foam. A mattress under the foot changed the leg above it.
move: Expect people to adjust when a device takes over part of their job.
trap: Assuming a softer sole must mean a softer landing for the body.

diagram.caption: The softer sole brought a harder landing: impact peak 10.7% higher.
